name: Brainiac
label: Touch and Go
lede: Four kids from Dayton with synths, noise and flashy 1970s stage clothes, who reportedly told Geffen where to go, got courted by Interscope, and lost their singer five days after he bought an old Mercedes.

eras.title: We'll Eat Anything
eras.text: Brainiac came out of Dayton, Ohio, the same small city as Guided by Voices and the Breeders, and sounded like neither. Within a year of their first show a major-label executive was calling.

years.p: Tim Taylor on vocals, keyboards and guitar, Juan Monasterio on bass, Michelle Bodine on guitar and Tyler Trent on drums start Brainiac in Dayton in January 1992.

years.h: First show, as We'll Eat Anything, at Wright State's Rathskellar
years.p: Brainiac's first gig is an opening slot for the Oxymorons at Wright State University's Rathskellar, played under the temporary name We'll Eat Anything.

years.h: Smack Bunny Baby, the debut album on Grass Records
years.p: Brainiac's first album comes out on the New York label Grass Records.

years.h: Brainiac reportedly turn down a £2 million Geffen offer
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Geffen's Gary Gersh offered Brainiac a £2 million deal soon after Smack Bunny Baby, and the band allegedly told him to fuck off.

years.h: Michelle Bodine leaves; John Schmersal joins on guitar
years.p: Michelle Bodine quits Brainiac in November 1993 and later leads O-matic and Shesus. [[John Schmersal|9f0f837b-e427-4611-aef4-5db88298bfaf]] takes over guitar, keyboards and backing vocals.

eras.title: Bonsai Superstar
eras.text: With Girls Against Boys' Eli Janney producing, Brainiac made records that broke on purpose: shorted mics, found voices, singing through a fan. Touch and Go signed them, Kim Deal produced them, and the tours got bigger.

years.h: Bonsai Superstar, produced by GVSB's Eli Janney
years.p: Brainiac record at Plantain Studios in Brooklyn with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] of [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]]. It's John Schmersal's first album with the band.
years.xp:
One song was cut in a basement with a cheap bullet mic that shorted out mid-vocal, leaving the feedback in the mix. Voice samples on another came from a record found in a Knoxville, Tennessee, store, and the chorus was sung into an electric fan to make it stutter.

According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork later ranked Bonsai Superstar No. 57 on its top 100 albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Lollapalooza side stage and a John Peel session
years.p: Brainiac play the Lollapalooza side stage and record four songs in the UK for BBC Radio 1's John Peel sessions.

years.h: Internationale EP, produced by Kim Deal, on Touch and Go
years.p: Brainiac sign to Touch and Go and release the Internationale EP, produced by [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] of [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] and the Pixies.

years.h: On the road with Beck, the Breeders and the Jesus Lizard
years.p: Brainiac's live shows build a buzz as they open tours for Beck, [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] and [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]].

eras.title: Saturday Night Fever gone punk
eras.text: Brainiac's Touch and Go album dressed the noise in flashy 1970s clothes and made them one of the most talked-about live bands in American indie rock. Elektra and Interscope started chasing them.

q: Make pop music that sounded futuristic so it wouldn't sound dated.
years.src: Wikipedia: Hissing Prigs in Static Couture
years.h: Hissing Prigs in Static Couture, Brainiac's last album
years.p: Mostly recorded at Water Music in Hoboken, New Jersey, with Eli Janney; Steve Albini cut "Nothing Ever Changes" in his basement. CMJ's Jenny Eliscu described Brainiac as Saturday Night Fever gone punk.
years.xp: The band went for a 1970s fashion-band look on stage, in flashy outfits. Magnet later called the album a lost classic.

eras.title: An EP, an Interscope deal, a 1972 Mercedes
eras.text: Brainiac cut a synth-heavy EP with Jim O'Rourke as a teaser for a major-label album. Weeks after it came out, Tim Taylor was dead at 28 and the band was over.

years.h: Electro-Shock for President, produced by Jim O'Rourke
years.p: Brainiac's six-song EP, produced and mixed by [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]], leans hard into synths. It was meant as a teaser for a fourth album on Interscope, where the band was reportedly about to sign.

years.h: Tim Taylor dies in his 1972 Mercedes, and Brainiac ends
years.p: Tim Taylor, 28, crashed his 1972 Mercedes into a lamppost, and the car caught fire. John Schmersal said toxicology showed carbon monoxide poisoning killed Taylor before the crash.
years.xp:
The documentary Transmissions After Zero showed the car had rusted badly enough to let exhaust leak into the passenger compartment. Taylor had bought it five days earlier.

A benefit show a few months later featured Dayton's [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]] and [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]].

eras.title: Rewiring other people's bands
eras.text: The survivors scattered into other projects while Brainiac's reputation grew without them. Trent Reznor, the Mars Volta, Muse and the National all pointed back to them, and a documentary finally told the story.

years.h: John Schmersal forms Enon; Tyler Trent joins the Breeders
years.p: John Schmersal makes a solo record as John Stuart Mill, then starts [[Enon|ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06]]. Tyler Trent briefly drums in [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]], and Juan Monasterio turns to directing music videos.

q: Would rewire your idea of a rock band.
years.h: Trent Reznor uses Electro-Shock for President as a guide for With Teeth
years.p: [[Trent Reznor|bc880664-6751-4998-984d-ebdbff15d229]] called Brainiac a major influence and used the Electro-Shock for President EP as a sound reference for [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]]' 2005 album With Teeth.
years.xp: Cedric Bixler-Zavala and Omar Rodríguez-López of [[At the Drive-In|7e13cd1c-0300-4d03-bd8e-5f86dd99d74f]] and [[The Mars Volta|20883363-1ea4-4d72-ad72-c0e767038f3e]] cited the same EP. Matt Bellamy said part of [[Muse|9c9f1380-2516-4fc9-a3e6-f9f61941d090]]'s "Exo-Politics" owed Brainiac a debt, and Chris Walla named them for [[Death Cab for Cutie|0039c7ae-e1a7-4a7d-9b49-0cbc716821a6]]'s Narrow Stairs.

years.h: Transmissions After Zero, the Brainiac documentary, premieres
years.p: Eric Mahoney's film tells Brainiac's story, with new performances in New York, Los Angeles and Dayton featuring singer Tim Krug. It came out on DVD and streaming on February 21, 2020.

eras.title: Back on stage with Mogwai
eras.text: Twenty-five years after Taylor's death, the other three put Brainiac back on stage with Tim Krug singing, and dug out unreleased demos.

years.h: Brainiac announce a UK tour supporting Mogwai
years.p: Juan Monasterio, Tyler Trent and John Schmersal, with Tim Krug on vocals and keys, set UK dates opening for [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]] in February 2023, plus their own headline shows.

years.h: The Predator Nominate EP of unreleased Brainiac demos
years.p: Brainiac release previously unheard demos with Tim Taylor on The Predator Nominate, ahead of the Mogwai tour.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Hissing Prigs in Static Couture
